record.paper_title: Recent results and open questions on collective type phenomena from A-A to pp collisions
record.original_question: Can a two-dimensional event-selection condition that combines charged-particle multiplicity with global event-shape observables such as Directivity, Sphericity, Thrust, or Fox-Wolfram moments reliably isolate soft, nearly azimuthally isotropic proton-proton events with specific azimuthal distributions at a given multiplicity?

evidence.quote: Studies along the possibility to select events close to azimuthal isotropy using global event shape observables like Directivity, Sphericity, Thrust or Fox-Wolfram moments have shown their performance in selecting soft, nearly azimuthal isotropic events [35, 36].

Although the correlations are rather good, it is clearly seen that even at the highest multiplicities the global event shape variables have a rather broad distribution. Therefore, a two dimensional condition in multiplicity and different event shape variables could signiﬁcantly contribute in selecting events with speciﬁc azimuthal distributions for a given multiplicity.
The selection of high multiplicity events close to azimuthal isotropy based on event shape global observables seems to be feasible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider proton–proton collision events at LHC energies. For each event, let the charged-particle multiplicity be N, and define the following global event-shape observables computed from the transverse momenta p⃗_T,i of the N charged particles in a chosen pseudorapidity acceptance:

- Transverse Sphericity S_T, defined via the smaller eigenvalue λ_2 of the 2×2 transverse momentum tensor
  M = (1/Σ|p⃗_T,i|) Σ_i (1/|p⃗_T,i|) (p_{x,i}^2, p_{x,i}p_{y,i}; p_{y,i}p_{x,i}, p_{y,i}^2),
  by S_T = 2λ_2/(λ_1+λ_2), so that S_T ∈ [0,1] with S_T → 0 for pencil-like and S_T → 1 for azimuthally isotropic events.
- Thrust T = max_{n̂} Σ_i |p⃗_T,i · n̂| / Σ_i |p⃗_T,i|.
- Directivity D, defined analogously as a normalized sum of projections onto a chosen reference direction.
- The Fox–Wolfram moments H_ℓ, ℓ = 0,1,2,…, computed from the angular distribution of final-state particles.

A "soft, azimuthally isotropic" event is one whose azimuthal distribution dN/dφ is consistent with rotational invariance up to statistical fluctuations and which contains no hard jet structure.

Question. Does there exist a two-dimensional event-selection criterion of the form (N, X) ∈ R, where X ∈ {S_T, T, D, H_ℓ} is one of the above event-shape variables and R is a region in the (multiplicity, event-shape) plane, such that the selected sub-sample at any fixed multiplicity N reliably consists of soft, nearly azimuthally isotropic events with prescribed azimuthal distributions, in the sense that residual contamination by hard, jetty events vanishes in a controlled way as the selection is tightened? Equivalently, can the broad spread of the conditional distribution of X at fixed N be overcome by a joint cut in (N, X) so as to isolate isotropic-topology events at high multiplicity?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent ALICE measurements and Monte Carlo studies (e.g., transverse spherocity-based selections at √s = 13 TeV, and "hedgehog" event analyses) have demonstrated that two-dimensional cuts combining multiplicity with transverse spherocity (or related event-shape variables) can effectively separate soft isotropic from hard jetty topologies, supporting feasibility. However, a fully model-independent characterization of the azimuthal distribution at fixed multiplicity remains an active area, with results being refined; the question is therefore partially addressed rather than definitively closed.

status_evidence.title: Light-flavor particle production in high-multiplicity pp collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Transverse spherocity estimator categorizes events by their azimuthal topology... narrow selections... contrast soft-dominated vs hard-scattering events.
status_evidence.claim: Two-dimensional (multiplicity, spherocity) selections successfully isolate soft, isotropic-topology pp events.

status_evidence.title: A look into the hedgehog events in pp collisions
status_evidence.snippet: High multiplicity pp collisions appear more isotropic (hedgehog-like) than predicted by MC generators.
status_evidence.claim: Selecting high-multiplicity isotropic events using event-shape observables is feasible and is being actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Event-shape- and multiplicity-dependent identified particle production in pp collisions at 13 TeV with ALICE
status_evidence.snippet: Event classifiers based on charged-particle multiplicity or event shape extensively used by ALICE.
status_evidence.claim: Combined multiplicity + event-shape selection has become a standard, working tool in pp collision analyses.
